sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Rowan County?
sections.html:
Rowan County Tax Administration has two divisions, the Assessor's office and the Tax Collector's office. The Assessor lists, assesses and bills all taxable property in the county, and the collector takes payment. The real property appraisers can be reached at 704-216-8586, and the county directs listing questions to 704-216-8558.

The county says it is building an electronic online listing process that should be ready for the 2027 listing season. Until then, ask the office how to list personal property, such as a boat, a camper or a mobile home, each January.

Rowan County is in the Salisbury area, and its Tax Assessor site includes a map tool for land records. Sellers there will deal with the county bill and with any municipal or district bill that applies to the parcel, so check the tax record for every levy before you list.

sections.h2: When does Rowan County revalue property?
sections.html:
Rowan County revalues every four years. The county's revaluation page says its last revaluation was January 1, 2023, the next takes effect January 1, 2027, and the following one is scheduled for January 2031.

State law only requires a reappraisal every eight years, and the county page explains the shorter cycle as a way to soften sticker shock between revaluations. The county also states that revaluation does not set tax rates, which the commissioners decide in the annual budget, and that values come from actual sales.

If you plan to sell in or near a revaluation year, expect buyers to look at the new assessed value, because it drives the bill they will inherit.

sections.h2: What is the COMPER tool for Rowan County owners?
sections.html:
COMPER is an online tool that shows the valid sales the tax office uses to help set values in the 2027 cycle. You enter a property address and receive a list and a map of valid sales between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2026 within a five-mile radius.

From that list you can pick sales similar to your home and turn them into a printable or PDF report. The map includes a street view of each comparable property. A Rowan County seller can use the same report to check a listing price against what the assessor treats as valid sales, though the tool does not replace an agent's or appraiser's opinion.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Rowan County property value?
sections.html:
Start by contacting the tax office informally, then file a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review if the difference is not settled. The county says informal appeals typically happen between January and March. The page also tells owners to complete the Real Property Appeal Form and return it with supporting documents, and it warns that an appeal may leave the value unchanged, lower it or raise it.

The county outlines the formal path as follows:

  • All real property appeals for a year must be received before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns.
  • The first meeting of the Board falls no earlier than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May, with the notice published in a local newspaper at least three times, the first at least 10 days before the meeting.
  • The Board gives each side time to present, may decide right away or take time to deliberate, and the taxpayer should receive the decision in writing.
  • Further appeal goes to the Property Tax Commission, which meets monthly in Raleigh, acts as a trial court and puts the burden of proof on the taxpayer. Corporate and LLC owners must use an attorney licensed in North Carolina.

Personal property is different. A taxpayer may appeal value, situs or taxability within 30 days after the initial notice of value, and if no separate notice is mailed, the tax bill is the notice. After adjournment the Board may continue to hear appeals on discovered property, classified motor vehicles, audits and personal property.

sections.h2: When are Rowan County taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due each September 1 under state law, and interest starts on January 6. The statute allows payment at face value until then, then adds two percent through February 1 and three-fourths of one percent each month after that.

A county can adopt a prepayment discount schedule by resolution before May 1, and Rowan County's own collector page would be the place to confirm whether one is in force for the current year. Ask the Tax Collector's office for the exact payment channels and any card fee, because those details are set locally.

Listing runs from the first business day of January through January 31, and the county commissioners may extend it. An owner who misses listing for personal property can expect a penalty, so file even if your list is short.

sections.h2: What relief programs can Rowan County owners use?
sections.html:
The state offers an elderly or disabled exclusion, a disabled veteran exclusion and a circuit breaker deferment, and Rowan County's revaluation page points owners to these three. The county has an Exemptions page for the forms. Only one program can be used by an owner.

  • Elderly or disabled: the greater of $25,000 or half of appraised value for a permanent residence, with a 2026 income limit of $38,800 as printed by the state.
  • Disabled veteran: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax capped at 4.0% or 5.0% of income depending on the income band, with excess deferred as a lien.

Applications go to the county assessor on Form AV-9. Under the circuit breaker, deferred taxes for the last three years come due if the home is sold or the owner dies or moves out, so a seller on that program should request a payoff from the Tax Collector early.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when I sell my Rowan County house?
sections.html:
They are paid at closing, because the lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date each year. Penalties, interest and costs attach with it, and a lien for personal property taxes can reach all of the taxpayer's real property in the taxing unit.

If taxes stay unpaid, the county can file a foreclosure action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure and sell the parcel at a public auction. Before confirmation, the owner may redeem by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

Ask the Rowan County Tax Collector for a written payoff on each parcel, then give it to your closing attorney. Owners with a quick sale in mind should check this first, because back taxes limit the price and timing options.

faqs.q: When is Rowan County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: The county's page says the next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, and that the following one is scheduled for January 2031 on a four-year cycle.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Rowan County assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the tax office informally first, then complete the Real Property Appeal Form with supporting documents and file it before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns. The Board's first meeting falls between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal personal property in Rowan County?
faqs.a: You have 30 days after the initial notice of value. If the assessor sends no separate notice, the tax bill counts as the notice of value.
COMPER is the county's online comparison tool. Enter an address to see valid sales from January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026 within five miles, and build a report from similar homes.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Rowan County Tax Assessor?
faqs.a: Real property appraisers are at 704-216-8586, and the county lists 704-216-8558 for listing questions. The office also has an email contact on its Tax Assessor page.
